source_license: Public — official government data. Verify terms of use with Fairfax County before commercial redistribution.
pilot_notes: Live-verified 2026-08-15 via six rounds of disposable diagnostic GitHub Actions dispatch, the same methodology used for Loudoun and Prince William. Three rounds enumerating Fairfax County's own ArcGIS Server host (www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator, 8 REST folders) found nothing -- the real zoning service is instead hosted on ArcGIS Online's shared infrastructure under Fairfax's own official org account (FX.AuthData, contentStatus 'public_authoritative'), findable only via an ArcGIS Online item search. Layer 0 ('Zoning') carries real fields ZONECODE/ZONETYPE/PROFFER/PUBLIC_LAND/JURISDICTION, geometryType esriGeometryPolygon, 6,440 features total -- but that spans THREE real jurisdictions merged into one layer (Fairfax County, Town of Herndon, Town of Vienna, plus a few null-jurisdiction records). The fetch pipeline is configured with a where clause (JURISDICTION='FAIRFAX COUNTY') to scope to the county only: 6,242 features, 0 with null/empty ZONECODE, 44 real distinct ZONECODE values, independently confirmed. Do not treat an absent or 'not_listed' classification as meaning data centers are prohibited -- it means the classification has not been researched yet.
known_limitations: 10 of 44 real district codes (C-3, C-4, I-2, I-3, I-4, I-5, I-6, PDC, PTC, PRC) now have data-center permitted-use research at moderate confidence (secondary-source corroboration, not raw ordinance text extraction -- see permitted_uses.json). The remaining 34 codes are honest not_listed placeholders.

The Zoning FeatureServer layer 0 has no separate district-name field -- ZONECODE is the only classification attribute. A coarse ZONETYPE grouping field exists (RESIDENTIAL/COMMERCIAL/INDUSTRIAL/PLANNED UNITS/OTHER/TYSON) but is not a per-code name and is not mapped into district_category for the 34 still-unresearched codes.

The same FeatureServer also carries Town of Herndon and Town of Vienna zoning under the same layer -- deliberately excluded from this jurisdiction's data via a where-clause filter (JURISDICTION='FAIRFAX COUNTY') rather than ingested as county data.

Dimensional standards (setbacks, height, FAR) are entirely unresearched for every district. The 2024 data-center amendment's own countywide setbacks (200 ft building / 300 ft ground equipment from a residential lot line) are recorded in permitted_uses.json's notes but not yet modeled as structured dimensional_standards entries.

PRC's 'prohibited' classification reflects county staff's proposal and the Board's September 2024 action as reported by secondary sources -- re-verify against the final adopted ordinance text if precision matters for a specific parcel.
notes: Third Virginia pilot jurisdiction after Loudoun and Prince William. Geometry pipeline proven end-to-end. Parcel-to-zoning spatial join now exists (js/parcel/zoning-geometry.js, built for all three NoVA counties). Data-center permitted-use research: 10 of 44 codes done at moderate confidence (2026-08-16); the other 34 remain the next step.
